content.title: About
content.content: Tortilla chips are crunchy slices made from corn or wheat tortillas that are fried or baked until golden. The reduced‑sodium version contains roughly 2‑3 times less salt than regular chips, making them a better choice for people watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortilla chips originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a convenient snack.
Corn chips are traditionally made from whole‑grain corn, making them naturally gluten‑free.
Reduced sodium is achieved by using special salt blends and lowering the amount of added salt.
Chips are often served with salsa, guacamole, or cheese dip.
Baked versions contain less fat than fried ones.

items.title: Low Sodium Content
items.content: Reduced sodium helps maintain normal blood pressure and eases the workload on the kidneys.

items.title: Source of Complex Carbohydrates
items.content: Corn chips provide slowly digestible carbs that give sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: Contains Fiber
items.content: Corn is a good source of dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chips are often fortified with thiamine, niacin, and folate, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Corn contains carotenoids such as lutein, which are beneficial for eye health.

items.title: High Calorie Density
items.content: Even with reduced sodium, chips are calorie‑dense and can contribute to weight gain if eaten in excess.

items.title: Fat Content
items.content: Fried varieties contain saturated and sometimes trans fats; baked versions are a healthier alternative.

items.title: Corn or Wheat Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to the primary grain used in the chips.

items.title: Additives and Flavorings
items.content: Certain products may contain artificial flavors or preservatives that not everyone tolerates well.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tortilla chips are perfect as a standalone snack, paired with dips, used in tacos, added to salads, or as a crunchy topping for casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent staleness.
